title: A toll at Aydhab
body: Hamza leads caravans to the Red Sea. A caravan is a group of travellers and animals that go together. At Aydhab a toll, a fee to pass, is taken on every load. Hamza asks every house that sends goods his way to pay a share.

choices.label: Pay a share of the toll
choices.hint: It costs now. Hamza will speak well of you.

choices.label: Send goods by Quseir instead
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars in two seasons, not 5 now. Quseir is nearer to Qus, and partners like a house that counts its costs.

note: Ibn Battuta saw Aydhab in 1326. One third of the town was the sultan's, and two thirds was the Beja king's. A writer of about 1400 says some merchants preferred Quseir, because it was nearer Qus.

sources.at: pp. 33 and 35; Quseir nearer Qus, and the split of Aydhab's revenue (sometimes in half)
vol. 1, p. 68; one third of the city the sultan's, two thirds the Beja king's, in 1326

title: The officer counts twice
body: Your carters wait at Alexandria to bring a merchant's goods up from a ship. A customs officer there has not met your house, so he counts every bundle twice. Customs are taxes on goods that enter a port. He asks for 5 dinars.

choices.label: Pay it all and ask for a receipt
choices.hint: It costs now. Your name goes in his book.

choices.label: Leave the goods in the harbour store
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars in two seasons, not 5 now. Your goods wait and the officer notices, but partners like a patient house.

note: A merchant's handbook from about 1340 says goods coming into Alexandria paid 20 in every hundred. Goods going out paid nothing.

sources.at: print p. 72; the duty at Alexandria

title: A stranger needs a name
body: Giorgio is new in Alexandria. The port officers do not know him, but they know your house. He asks you to vouch for him, to tell them he will pay what he owes. If he does not pay, they will come to you.

choices.label: Vouch for Giorgio
choices.hint: It costs 5 in two seasons. He will not forget it. His debt could become yours.

choices.label: Say you do not know him
choices.hint: You keep your money. The port officers like a house that knows whom it vouches for.

note: Merchants had long done favours for each other and expected the same. One Geniza letter says: "you are in my place there, for you know well that I am your support here."

sources.at: p. 316; business friends who serve each other

title: Papers for the road
body: Nabil belongs to the Karimi, a loose group of merchants who trade spices. One writer says a spice office gave them papers for the road. It took 2.5 in every hundred of their goods. He says he could carry two loads for your house under his papers.

choices.label: Send two loads under his papers
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars for the papers. Nabil will be glad to help.

choices.label: Go without his papers
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars in two seasons, not 5 now. Nabil may feel left out, but the officers see your own count.

note: One modern writer says the Karimi office gave its members papers. He says it took 2.5 in every hundred of their goods. The Karimi were a loose group, and historians do not agree on how tightly they were organised.

sources.at: pp. 150 and 152; a loose confederation; the office's papers and 2.5 percent are al-Ashqar's reading, as Sato reports it, and Sato takes the office for a state one

title: Small tolls on the Nile
body: Nuh takes goods up the Nile from Cairo to Qus. At each town on the way a small toll is paid, a fee to pass. He asks you to pay each toll as the boat goes, so it is never held up.

choices.label: Pay each toll as the boat goes
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. Nuh says your house is easy to work with.

choices.label: Pay all the tolls at the end
choices.hint: It costs 1 dinar now and 2 more in two seasons, for paying late. Nuh does not mind.

choices.label: Use a rival's boat
choices.hint: It costs nothing now. Nuh is hurt, and he remembers it.

note: In a lawsuit of 1097, a merchant said he paid small dues in the towns on the Nile. At Akhmim and Qus each was one eighth of a dinar, 227 years before 1324.

title: A list of customs
body: Isaac sends a list from Aydhab. Customs are taxes on goods that enter a port, and the list shows what each good pays. Frankincense pays a third of a dinar. He asks how you want the fees paid.

choices.label: Pay as the list says
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. Isaac sends his accounts in two seasons, and foreign houses think well of you.

choices.label: Ask the officials for a lower rate
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now, for gifts to the officials. They do not forget it.

choices.label: Pay part now and the rest later
choices.hint: It costs 1 dinar now and 4 more in three seasons. Your partners like a house that pays in the end.

note: In a list written about 1152, a merchant noted the fees on five goods carried from Aden to Aydhab. Frankincense paid a third of a dinar in customs there.

title: The water is cut off
body: Amin lives in Aden. Bedouins, people of the desert, have blocked the way to the town's water tanks. They let people through only for money and cloth. Amin asks you to share the cost.

choices.label: Share the cost in cloth and coin
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. The town has water, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Pay in coin only
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. Amin thanks you, and your partners hear of it.

choices.label: Bring water by sea
choices.hint: It costs 12 dinars now. The court at Aden is grateful.

note: At Aden the bedouins often cut off the way to the water tanks. They kept the townspeople from the water until they bought the bedouins' consent with money and cloth.

title: The ruler's men signal
body: A ship of yours passes a town on the Malabar coast. The ruler's men signal it to anchor and give a present. The pilot asks what to do.

choices.label: Anchor and give the present
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. The ship sails on safe, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Sail on
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and 10 dinars in two seasons, when the ruler's men chase the ship and tax it double. The ship does reach market early, and partners like that.

choices.label: Change course to keep clear
choices.hint: It costs 7 dinars now, for the longer way. The court hears that you avoid trouble.

note: On the Malabar coast every ship passing a town had to anchor and give the ruler a present, the right of dandar. A ship that did not was chased, brought in by force, and taxed double.

title: Pepper in public warehouses
body: Zaid writes from Calicut. The town keeps its pepper in public warehouses and sells it by the bahar, a large weight. The customs are two parts in every ten. He asks if you will ship now.

choices.label: Pay the customs and ship
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The goods go safe, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Ship from Quilon by a longer road
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. The road is long, but foreign houses like it.

choices.label: Wait
choices.hint: It costs nothing. Zaid sells to another house.

note: A Chinese traveller, Wang Ta-yuan, wrote in 1330 that Calicut stored pepper in public warehouses and sold it by the bahar. He said the customs were two parts in every ten.

sources.at: pp. 294 to 295 (Wang Ta-yuan, Tao i chih lio, in Rockhill's translation)

title: The king taxes copper
body: A copper dealer says the king of Mali taxes the raw copper brought in from the mine at Takedda. The tax is heavy. He asks if your house will pay it and take a share of the copper.

choices.label: Pay the tax
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The court of Mali thinks well of your house.

choices.label: Hide the copper from the tax men
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and 5 dinars in two seasons, a fine if the tax men find it. Partners dislike a cheat.

choices.label: Decline the share
choices.hint: It costs nothing. The dealer sells to another house.

note: In 1324 Mansa Musa reportedly told a scholar in Cairo that raw copper from Takedda earned him more tax than anything else. Al-Umari wrote it down.

title: Silver bars for the mint
body: A Venetian buyer pays you in silver bars. The sultan's mint at Alexandria turns bars into coins for a fee. Some merchants the sultan favours pay a lower fee.

choices.label: Take the silver to the mint
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now, the mint fee. Foreign merchants see that you pay what is owed.

choices.label: Ask a court friend for the lower fee
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now, a gift to the friend. The court thinks well of you.

choices.label: Sell the bars to a goldsmith
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now, a low price. It is quick, and partners like quick money.

note: About 1310 a Venetian wrote that the sultan's mint charged 6 and two thirds in 100 to coin gold. It charged 4 and a half for silver, and 3 and a half for favoured merchants.

title: A lower duty on silver
body: The sultan's clerk says the tax on gold and silver, coming in or going out, is now 2 in 100. It was higher before. He asks if you will bring in silver.

choices.label: Bring in a large load of silver
choices.hint: It costs 10 dinars now. The saving shows later, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Bring in a small trial load
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. It is a small risk, and partners like it.

choices.label: Wait to see if the rate holds
choices.hint: It costs nothing. If the clerk goes back on it, you lost nothing.

note: The treaty of 1345 set the tax on gold and silver, coming in or going out, at 2 in 100. Before that, gold coming in paid 4 in 100, and silver 3 and a half.

title: Whose name on the goods
body: Orhan trades at Constantinople. Genoese and Venetians there pay no customs, and others pay 2 in 100. He asks under whose name your goods should go.

choices.label: Ship as a Genoese partner's goods
choices.hint: It costs 10 dinars now, a share for the Genoese. You pay no customs, and foreign houses think well of you.

choices.label: Ship under your own name
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now, the customs. The court of the city notes that you pay.

choices.label: Sell in Pera instead
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. The buyer is near, and partners like a quick sale.

note: At Constantinople the Genoese and Venetians paid no customs, and Pisans paid 2 in 100 each way. Florentines and others paid 2 in 100 once, on a paper good for one year.

title: Which people own the ship
body: A customs man at Famagusta asks which people your ship belongs to. The king of Cyprus charges each people a different rate.

choices.label: Declare Genoese partners
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now, a share for the partners. You pay no customs.

choices.label: Declare Pisan
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now, 2 in 100 each way. Partners think it fair.

choices.label: Declare Florentine
choices.hint: It costs 6 dinars now, the dearest rate. The court notes your honesty.

note: In Cyprus the Genoese and Venetians paid no customs. Pisans and some others paid 2 in 100 each way, and Florentines usually paid 4.

title: The duty at Tunis
body: Piero ships goods to Tunis. He says Christians there pay 10 in every 100 on all they bring in. He asks how you want your goods shipped.

choices.label: Pay the standard duty
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The goods are accepted, and the court thinks well of you.

choices.label: Ship under a Venetian partner
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now, the same duty. You owe the partner a favour, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Ship by a later boat
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. Your profit comes slowly, and partners wait.

note: At Tunis Christians paid 10 in 100 on everything they brought in. Venetians paid 10, and Florentines 10 and a half, with about 1 more for clerks.

sources.at: Pagnini 1766 printing, p. 123 (the duty on goods)

title: The post at Qatya
body: A caravan of yours has reached Qatya, a frontier post on the road to Syria. Goods are searched there and the alms tax is collected. No one may pass without a passport from the other country.

choices.label: Turn back and ask a friend for a pass
choices.hint: It costs 3 dinars now. A season is lost, but the goods are safe, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Pay the officials extra
choices.hint: It costs 8 dinars now. The goods pass, foreign houses hear of it, and the court notes your name.

choices.label: Wait at an inn for a courier
choices.hint: It costs 2 dinars now. The wait is long, and your people grow tired.

note: On the road from Cairo to Syria, Qatya was a frontier post where goods were examined and the alms tax collected. No one could pass without a passport from the other country.

title: Guards of the desert road
body: Bedouins who guard the desert road ask a payment from your caravan. The sultan pays them too. Your guide asks what to do.

choices.label: Pay them
choices.hint: It costs 5 dinars now. Your goods pass safe, and foreign houses hear of it.

choices.label: Hire your own guards
choices.hint: It costs 9 dinars now. You owe nobody, and partners like that.

choices.label: Go without a guard
choices.hint: It costs nothing now and 8 dinars in two seasons, if raiders find the caravan. Your people admire your nerve.

note: The sultan paid Bedouin tribes to guard the post and trade roads, and the tribes also took payments from merchants. In 1340 the sultan ruled that merchants must ask his permission to use state relay stations.

title: The toll bill from Ayas
body: A trader at Tabriz sends the toll bill for the road from Ayas. Tolls are fees to pass. There is one at nearly every stage, and Mongol horsemen take more on top.

choices.label: Pay as asked
choices.hint: It costs 9 dinars now. There is no delay, and partners hear of it.

choices.label: Haggle at each stage
choices.hint: It costs 4 dinars now. Each stage takes time, and your people tire of it.

choices.label: Choose another route
choices.hint: It costs 7 dinars now. The way is new, and foreign houses hear of it.

note: On the road from Ayas to Tabriz a merchant paid a small toll at nearly every stage. Mongol horsemen took about 50 aspers a load on top.
